sources.title: Interview note containing the contiguous Fibonacci-string partition question
Deterministic Java validation against a recursive all-partitions oracle
Source-first isolated review for the Fibonacci-string candidate

claims.text: The recovered source restricts the input alphabet to 1-9, requires a contiguous partition of the whole string into at least three numbers satisfying the Fibonacci recurrence, and returns Boolean; it does not preserve a maximum length or integer-width contract.

After choosing the first two cuts, every later numeric segment is uniquely determined as the decimal representation of the sum of the preceding two values, so a mismatch at the current input position proves that split pair cannot succeed.

BigInteger is an explicit candidate implementation choice that avoids introducing an unstated int/long overflow boundary; its memory and arithmetic costs grow with digit width and are not presented as source requirements.

The exact Java implementation passes eight fixed cases including a value beyond long range and 5000 deterministic randomized 1-9 strings against a recursive all-partitions oracle, while enforcing complete input consumption.

findings: The candidate is source-bounded and separates source facts from API/numeric implementation choices.
The forced-suffix invariant is sufficient to justify pruning once the first two terms are selected.
Complete input consumption and the minimum-three-term condition are explicit in both the algorithm and proof.
The recursive partition oracle is structurally different from the candidate and covers 5000 deterministic randomized source-domain inputs.
The arbitrary-precision fixed case verifies the candidate does not depend on an unstated long boundary.
No online-judge attribution, hidden size bound or fabricated project claim was introduced.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the pilot human-approval gate.
